Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> HP News 9 | National UN welcomes Kofi Annan’s appearance on new GH¢100 banknote Source : Ernest K. Arhinful 13 November 2026 5:47am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The United Nations in Ghana has welcomed the decision to feature former UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan on the Bank of Ghana’s newly introduced GH¢100 banknote, describing it as recognition of his enduring contribution to global peace and diplomacy.
In a statement issued on Thursday, November 12, 2026, UN Resident Coordinator for Ghana, Zia Choudhury, said the tribute honoured a Ghanaian whose influence and work extended far beyond the country's borders.
Mr Annan served as the United Nations' seventh Secretary-General from 1997 to 2006, championing peace, human rights, sustainable development and international cooperation.
The UN said his leadership and commitment to multilateralism had left a lasting imprint on the organisation and the international community.
“His recognition on Ghana’s national currency is a fitting tribute to a distinguished son of Ghana whose contributions transcended national boundaries,” the statement said.
It added that the decision offered an opportunity to encourage younger generations to uphold the values of integrity, service, dialogue and global solidarity associated with Mr Annan’s leadership.
The GH¢100 denomination highlights Ghana’s contribution to international peace and diplomacy, with Mr Annan’s portrait appearing on the front. The reverse features the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre, alongside the Adinkra symbol Bi Nka Bi, which represents peaceful coexistence and the avoidance of conflict.
The banknote is part of the Bank of Ghana’s newly introduced Heritage Series, which comprises eight denominations celebrating prominent Ghanaian personalities, historical landmarks, and traditional symbols.
President John Mahama unveiled the new banknotes on Thursday, November 12, with each denomination reflecting a different aspect of Ghana’s history and national identity, including commerce, religious diversity, education, justice, culture, freedom, international peace and sovereignty.
At the launch, the President said the personalities and symbols featured on the notes would bring Ghana’s history closer to younger generations and deepen their appreciation of the country’s heritage.
The UN reaffirmed its commitment to promoting the values embodied in Mr Annan’s legacy and working with Ghana towards a more peaceful, inclusive and sustainable world.
